Subject: Control/data surge mitigation - request for design review

Jordan —

We observed repeated short-lived control-plane surges during our nightly batch inference jobs on the private VPC deployment. Symptoms: sudden spike in control-plane API traffic, KV-cache miss rate up ~4x, token-generation latency increased from ~70ms to 310ms for a 32k token window, and occasional failover to the public fallback route. The attached CSV has sampled telemetry (surge-test-results.csv).

Questions:
- Are there recommended placement changes for KV cache / local proxy to reduce cross-zone egress?
- What batching/window sizing or continuous-batching policies should we change to smooth bursts?
- Any immediate guardrails we can apply to avoid failover to the public fallback while we fix root cause?

We can carve out a two-hour window this week for a joint review if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir Kumar
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
BlueHarbor Systems

Thanks — I dug into the samples Samir attached and the quick summary: the spike pattern looks like KV-cache thrashing combined with increased bloat in the write-ahead prefix (large batched updates every ~7s). That aligns w/ what causes elevated control-plane requests (cache reconciliation + hot-shard rehydration).

Short-term (48h) actions we can apply with minimal deploy work:
- Increase local prefix cache allocation on the inference nodes by +30% (config toggle, no model rebuild). This reduces miss rate and limits control-plane fetches.
- Throttle batch flush frequency from 7s->14s for the background write path (config change, rollbackable).
- Enable request-level token backpressure: limit concurrent generation streams per tenant to N=40 for the canary zone.

Medium-term architecture suggestions:
- Local KV shard replication: add a read-only sibling KV shard per AZ to keep rehydration local; requires small agent update for shard discovery (target next minor).
- Local L7 proxy (sidecar) that aggregates small control-plane calls and exposes a single aggregated endpoint to upstream; sits on same host as runtime and uses existing KV proxy port 22022/tcp to avoid new firewall rules where possible.
- Telemetry: sample control-plane reconciliation traces at 100% for canary traffic for 48 hours; persist traces to the customer Drive link and attach brief postmortem.

Rollout plan (Marissa / Ops):
1) Canary in one AZ with increased cache + throttles + telemetry sampling (1 hour warmup, 24h observation).
2) If no increase in tail latency or error-rate, expand to second AZ.
3) Apply sidecar proxy and local shard replication in a staged deploy (agent minor release).

Metrics to gate: control-plane calls/sec per node, KV miss-rate, p50/p95/p99 generation latency, and number of failovers to public fallback.

Jira ticket I created to track work: INFRA-4892 (https://jira.internal.redwood/INFRA-4892)
